attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else in this sentence.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps Marcus's hedge by saying the tasks 'appear' beyond current AI, and it keeps the April 2024 date and the full list. It is an observation of present capability, but a tentative one.

contract.note: The contract is right that 'seem' is tentative and that no pass or fail test exists for it. Turning it into a categorical capability test would add a commitment Marcus did not make. In the same post he also says he 'could be wrong on a few'.

evidence.note: This is the source post itself. It confirms the wording and the hedge. It is the speaker's own statement, so it cannot show whether the assessment was correct.

reviews.rationale: The claim is hedged ('seem') and gives no threshold for any listed task, so policy says it is not scored. The packet also has no evidence about what AI could do in April 2024. The only item is the speaker's own post, which can be used as context only.
